question: Veer bought some sharpeners at the rate of ₹180/dozen. He sold them for ₹23 each. His profit percentage is ______% (rounded off to two decimal places).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Cost Price (CP) of 1 sharpener = 180 ÷ 12 = ₹15

Selling Price (SP) of 1 sharpener = ₹23

Profit = 23 − 15 = ₹8

Profit % = (8 ÷ 15) × 100 = 53.33%

**∴ The correct answer is 53.33%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost Price of a dozen (12) sharpeners = ₹180

Selling Price of 1 sharpener = ₹23

**Formula Used:**

Profit = SP − CP

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

 
 CP = ₹15
 
 
 + Profit = ₹8

 

 Selling Price (SP) = ₹23

 

 

 Profit = 53.33% of CP

**Calculations:**

⇒ CP of 1 sharpener = 180 ÷ 12 = ₹15

⇒ Profit = 23 − 15 = ₹8

⇒ Profit % = (8 ÷ 15) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (8 × 20) ÷ 3

⇒ Profit % = 160 ÷ 3 = 53.33%

**∴ The correct answer is 53.33%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Loss Percentage

If the selling price is less than the cost price, the loss % is calculated as: Loss % = [(CP − SP) ÷ CP] × 100.

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). SP = MP − Discount. Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100.

Successive Percentage Changes

For two successive changes of a% and b%, the effective percentage change is given by: (a + b + ab ÷ 100)%.
